Search and filters by category and tags
Backup and restore as .zip, done right in the browser

about.intro: I'm Marcelo — a backend developer who likes predictable systems: tested, observable and easy to ship.
full: Since July 2025 I've been a fullstack developer at Triveni Holding, maintaining and evolving .NET applications with Entity Framework and Vue, with Docker, SonarQube and Scrum as part of the daily routine.

Before that I spent almost four years as a QA Analyst at Skychart: test automation with Cypress, SQL to fix and validate data coming from external APIs, and scripts to automate the team's chores. That QA background shapes how I code — integration tests against a real database, measuring before optimizing, and documented decisions.

Outside work I build complete systems to go deep into backend: microservices with messaging and Kubernetes, an electronic health record with LGPD-grade auditing, and a foreign-trade ERP in Clean Architecture.

projects.title: Systems I've built
projects.intro: Eight complete projects, with architecture, tests and infrastructure. Each diagram shows how the pieces talk — hover a component to see its connections.

shipproof.name: ShipProof
shipproof.description: A task manager for development teams that doesn't trust “Done”: it follows branch, commits, pull request, merge and deploy, and only declares a task shipped when Git proves it. Integrates with GitHub and GitLab and receives tickets from the IT Service Desk.
highlights: Signed (HMAC), idempotent webhooks processed by a worker with a queue and outbox in PostgreSQL
Publication engine with configurable rules: merge, deploy or production pipeline
Over 200 tests (unit, integration against real Postgres and E2E) and a security audit with all 25 findings handled

orderflow.name: OrderFlow
orderflow.description: An event-driven ordering platform: three Spring Boot services talking over RabbitMQ, with MongoDB and an nginx gateway — later moved to a Kubernetes cluster with a pipeline that tests, publishes the image, deploys and rolls itself back if something goes wrong.
highlights: Rolling update with 148 out of 148 requests answered and zero failures
Automatic rollback in the pipeline when a deploy doesn't become healthy
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) and retry validated across three failure scenarios

pep.name: PEP — Electronic Health Record
pep.description: A multi-clinic electronic health record: patients, visits, prescriptions, exams and scheduling, with role-based access and an audit trail that records even who merely viewed a record.
highlights: Immutable audit: triggers block UPDATE/DELETE and a SHA-256 hash exposes tampering
JWT with rotating refresh and reuse detection, RBAC and per-clinic isolation
N+1 removed from scheduling: p95 from ~3.5 s to ~670 ms under load (k6)

tradingcomex.name: TradingComex
tradingcomex.description: A trading and foreign-trade ERP built module by module — partners, a catalogue with NCM codes, contracts with Incoterms 2020, logistics, customs documents (DI, DU-E) and FX — where every rule maps to a real market or legal requirement.
highlights: Clean Architecture with DDD: a pure C# domain with no infrastructure dependency
587 backend tests with xUnit, plus 116 on the frontend
Value Objects mapped in EF Core and validation in three layers

minoru.name: Minoru
minoru.description: The API of a productivity and personal-finance app: finances with PDF and CSV reports, kanban, AI study sessions (Gemini), notebooks and a blog — with background jobs, Google sign-in and end-to-end monitoring.
highlights: Self-hosted observability: OpenTelemetry feeding Tempo, Prometheus and Loki in Grafana
Over 750 tests, with integration against real PostgreSQL via Testcontainers
Load testing with k6 and benchmarks with BenchmarkDotNet

helpdesk.name: IT Service Desk
helpdesk.description: A GLPI-style IT ticketing system: tickets with attachments, handling with internal notes, full history, SLA per priority and category, role-based dashboards and reports — and handing tickets over to the development team in ShipProof.
highlights: ShipProof integration: a ticket becomes a task and its status comes back through a signed webhook
Idempotent SLA jobs guarded by a PostgreSQL advisory lock
Over 140 tests and a security audit: Argon2id, sealed sessions, CSRF and rate limiting

cardapio.name: Digital Menu
cardapio.description: An online menu for restaurants, with cart, checkout and an admin panel. Orders reach the kitchen in real time and product images live in S3-compatible storage.
highlights: Real-time orders over SSE, with reconnection and backoff on the client
232 backend tests (87% coverage) and 152 on the frontend
A refresh-token collision bug caught by the tests and fixed with jti

sightline.name: Sightline
sightline.description: Peer-to-peer screen sharing in the browser: create a room, send the link, and your screen goes straight to the other participants over WebRTC. The Node.js server only does signaling — it never sees your screen.
highlights: Multi-party mesh with the “perfect negotiation” pattern and automatic ICE restarts
WebSocket reconnection with session resume, and STUN/TURN with short-lived credentials
About 170 Vitest tests plus E2E with real WebRTC in the browser (Playwright); CI on Node 22 and 24
